title: Kerala Senior Citizens' Act 2026 passed unanimously; ‘World's first law that guarantees rights of senior citizens,’ says CM
content: Kerala Senior Citizens' (Care and Protection of Rights) Bill, 2026, which attempts to balance care and protection of senior citizens with the creation of a silver economy in which the elders 'constructively and creatively' contribute to the state's economy, was unanimously passed in the Assembly on Monday. Nearly 1300 amendments were moved by the members during the discussion on the Bill in the Assembly. "It is for the first time in the world that a law has been passed that guarantees the rights of senior citizens. There is no such guarantee in the Central Act (Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007) or the Act passed by Kerala before (Kerala State Senior Citizens Commission Act, 2025)," Chief Minister V D Satheesan said in the Assembly. Members had raised two major concerns about the Bill. One, the Bill has provisions that were inconsistent with certain clauses in the central Act. Two, the Bill has left out certain precautions laid down by the Supreme Court for drawing up a 'living will', particularly the mandatory presence of two independent witnesses. 'Living will' conundrum The 'living will' issue was flagged by former ministers K N Balagopal and K Rajan. They said that in the Bill, the 'living will' declaration could be made in the presence of the Chairperson of the District-Level Senior Citizen Protection Forum or the District-Level Senior Citizen Protection Unit. The need for two independent witnesses, as laid down by the Supreme Court, has been avoided. Living Will is the declaration in writing expressing the wish of a senior citizen at home or in any senior citizen care centre, that states his/her preferred 'end of life' priorities such as avoidance of life-extending surgery, IV fluids, chemotherapy, oxygen, admission in intensive care unit, use of invasive tubes and other medical aids. In Common Cause vs Union of India, the Supreme Court had said that the 'living will' should be signed in the presence of two independent witnesses and further countersigned by a Judicial Magistrate, First Class (JMFC) designated by the District Judge. The members felt that in the absence of independent witnesses, the execution of the 'living will' was liable to be hijacked by vested interests. The Chief Minister said that such fears were misplaced. "Members say that certain conditions laid down by the Supreme Court regarding the execution of 'living will' are not in this Bill. It is wrong. The fear was born out of a misreading of Clause 28 of the Bill (that deals with the execution of 'living will')," the CM said. He said that the members had failed to notice the phrase that came after the mention of "the Chairperson of the District Level Senior Citizen Protection Forum or the District Level Senior Citizen Protection Unit concerned". "Right after this, the clause says 'in the format and manner as prescribed'," the CM said. "It simply means that the protections prescribed by the Supreme Court will be laid down in the Rules for the Act," the CM said and pointed to clause 2(za) of the Act, which says "prescribed means "prescribed by rules made under this Act." "The Supreme Court guidelines will not be violated," the CM said. Toll-free number & MLA challenge During the discussion, Muslim League MLA P K Firos wanted a toll-free number to which senior citizens can call in times of distress. The Chief Minister said that the government would definitely consider the proposal while making the Rules for the Act. The Chief Minister also threw a challenge at members. "I am sure that MLAs can create model projects (for senior citizens) in your constituencies. You should think of it, discuss with concerned local bodies, and come up with projects that can inspire senior citizens to become constructive and creative rather than slump down, without any motivation, on an easy chair," he said, and added: "I promise you that if you come up with exemplary projects, the state will adopt these projects," the CM said...
